mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of sustained UNRATE increases above 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in demand and construction, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST are above their 12-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over two consecutive months indicates a loosening monetary policy alongside falling inflation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL decline for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 new jobs per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which increases consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 new jobs for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 3% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when RSAFS declines by more than 3% year-over-year (t-test p > 0.05).
